ECO2021 Basic Macroeconomics

                   Midterm Exam

                      Term1 2023/24


                Name__________________________

                 Student ID______________________



Instructions:

        1.  This is a closed-book exam. You have 60 minutes to complete the exam
           independently.
        2.  All questions are multiple choices questions. Maximum total point for this
        exam is 30 (1 point for each question).
        3.  Please mark your choices in the separate answer sheet provided using a
            pencil. Only the answer sheet will be graded.
        4.  Choose only one answer, the best answer.
        5. You can bring a simple calculator (non-programmable, and without the
            ability to store text), pencil, and other stationaries to the exam. Other
           electronic devices, books, notes, papers not provided by the exam organizer,
         and any means of communicating or accessing outside material are NOT
      ALLOWED during the exam.
        6.  If you have any questions about English words or clarification of the
           questions, you can raise your hand to ask the proctors.
        7.  After the exam, you must return in all the materials provided, including the
        exam questions, answer sheet, and scratch papers. No paper is allowed to be
          taken away with you.
        8. Make sure that your student ID  is written correctly in each document
           submitted. Unidentified answer sheets will not be graded.
        9.  Note that any violation of academic integrity, including policies from the
          course instructor, SME, and the university, may result in a failure grade for
           the course. If you are unclear about the exam policies, please confirm with
          an exam proctor.



Good Luck!

Basic Macroeconomics – Midterm Test


30 multiple choice questions – 60 minutes allowed.

Answer all questions. Choose only one answer, the best answer.


1.     The data in the table below is for a simple closed economy. Using the data in the table, what is the
        labor force participation rate for this economy equal to?

                     Total population                 20,000
                   Working-age population          15,000
                  Employment                     1,000
                 Unemployment                  100

      A.  (1,000/1,100) × 100%
       B.  (1,000/15,000) × 100%
       C.  (1,100/15,000) × 100%
      D.  (1,100/20,000) × 100%
       E.  (15,000/20,000) × 100%
C

2.      Indicate the reason why an economist would agree or disagree with the following statement: “In
        those years when stock or share purchases by households are high, investment will be high, and
        therefore, GDP will also be high.”
      A. Agree: When investment is high, people must have more money to spend. Therefore, GDP
             increases.
       B.  Disagree: Investment as a component of GDP refers to the purchase of physical and human
             capital and inventory, not purchases of stock or shares.
       C.  Disagree: While GDP will be high in this case, it is the result of an increase in consumer
           spending on stocks, not investment spending.
      D. Agree: GDP = C + I + G + NX. Therefore, when “I” (Investment) increases, GDP increases.
       E.  Disagree: When investment (I) increases, consumption (C) decreases, so GDP falls.
B

3.    Which of the following is NOT included as expenditure (C+I+G+NX) when calculating GDP?

      A. Wheat flour used by consumers at home.
       B.  Electronic toys produced in the country to be exported for sale abroad.
       C.  Electricity used by a toy company to run its machinery.
      D. Computers bought by the toy company for use by their accounting staff.
       E.  Electricity used by households for air conditioning at home.
C

4.    Why do economists believe that setting a goal of zero percent unemployment is not feasible or even
        desirable?

      A. Because technology keeps on improving, workers will keep on losing their jobs as the economy
           does not need as many workers are before.
       B. Many people retire each year and therefore they become unemployed, this will increase the
          unemployment rate.
       C. The economy will always experience cyclical unemployment even if the economy were
            operating at full productive capacity, at the full-employment level of output.
      D. Workers need time to find the right job, and companies need time to find the right worker. So,
            the economy needs some short-term unemployment in order to allow for better matching of jobs
           with workers that possess the proper skill set.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
D


                                                                                                2

5.     Describing the situation in England in 1920, the historian Robert Skidelsky wrote the following:
     “Who would not borrow at 4 percent a year, with prices going up 4 percent a month?” If these
       numbers are correct, what was the annual real interest rate paid by borrowers in this situation?

      A.  8%
       B.  0%
       C. 4%
      D. 44%
       E.  56%
E

6.      In macroeconomics, crowding out of investment occurs when:
      A. firms borrow more to expand operations, which results in an increase in interest rates, which in
            turn will reduce investment.
       B.  the government has a budget deficit and must borrow funds, which causes interest rates to rise,
          and thus private investment is reduced.
       C.  interest rates are increased by the Central Bank because it wants to reduce the economy’s money
            supply.
      D. firms spend a larger amount of resources on research and development, which increases
            technological progress, which reduces the demand for investment.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
B

7.     Suppose that during one historical period, the velocity of money is constant and during another
         historical period, it undergoes large fluctuations. During which period will the quantity theory of
      money be more useful in explaining changes in the inflation rate?

      A. The period where velocity is constant; because when velocity is constant, changes in the money
           supply can be shown to be the main cause of inflation.
       B. The period where velocity is constant; because according to the quantity equation, when velocity
               is constant, real output is the only variable that can affect prices.
       C. The period where velocity has large fluctuations; because the quantity equation can be used to
         show how money is the main determinant of inflation, even when velocity is fluctuating.
      D. The period where velocity has large fluctuations; because the quantity theory tells us that
            velocity is the main cause of inflation.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
A

8.     Your grandfather earned $7,000 per year at his first job in 1971. You earned $35,000 per year at
       your first job in 2021. Average prices (measured by CPI) have risen steadily since 1971. Which of
        the following statements is true?

      A. You earn exactly 5 times as much as your grandfather in terms of real income.
       B. You earn more than 5 times as much as your grandfather in terms of real income.
       C. You earn less than 5 times as much as your grandfather in terms of real income.
      D. You earn less than 5 times as much as your grandfather in terms of nominal income.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
C

9.    Which of the following would be a consequence of substitution bias in the CPI?

      A. Social Security payments (payments to retired people) would not adequately compensate retired
           workers for inflation.
       B.  Businesses would over-compensate employees for inflation when giving them cost of living
            adjustments.
       C. The inflation rate based on the CPI would under-estimate the true level of inflation.
      D. Judges would award child support payments that would not adequately keep up with the true cost
            of inflation.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
B

                                                                                                3

10.    Refer to the graph below which illustrates the market for loanable funds. Which of the following
         situations is consistent with the graph depicted?





      A. New technology has become available, and opportunities for profitable investments have
            increased.
       B. The government has reduced transfer payments to households, in order to decrease the
          government budget deficit.
       C. Households have increased the proportion of household income used for consumption (the
           marginal propensity to consume has increased).
      D.  Political uncertainty has worsened business confidence, and firms decide to cut back on
            investments.
       E.  There has been an increase in tax revenues collected by the government.
C

11.    Suppose that US commercial banks have $100 million in checking and savings account deposits, and
         that they hold no excess reserves. The required reserve ratio is 10 percent. Suppose that the Federal
       Reserve (the US central bank) reduces the required reserve ratio from 10 percent to 8 percent. As a
         result of this change, what would be the a maximum increase in the total amount of loans made by
     US commercial banks?
      A.  $2 million.
       B.  $8 million.
       C.  $10 million.
      D.  $25 million.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
D

12.    Consider an island nation, where taro root is the main food crop, and it is produced using a constant
        returns to scale technology (with diminishing marginal returns to individual inputs). Labor and land
        are the only inputs used for taro production. Which of the following must be true?

      A.  If the number of workers is doubled then 1.414 times as much taro will be produced.
       B.  If the number of workers is the same, but the amount of land used is halved, then half as much
            taro will be produced.
       C.  If the number of workers and amount of land used is doubled, then four times as much taro will
          be produced.
      D.  If the number of workers used is increased by 10%, then taro production will increase, but by
             less than 10%.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
D


                                                                                                4

13.    Marge is lending Arthur $1,000 for one year. The CPI is 160 at the time the loan is made. They
        expect it to be 176 in one year. If Marge and Arthur agree that Marge should earn about a 3% real
        return for the year, the nominal interest rate on this loan should be

      A. 3%
       B. 7%
       C. 10%
      D. 13%
       E. 17%
 D

14.      If government purchases are $400 million, taxes are $700 million, and transfers to households are
       $200 million, which of the following is true?
      A. Public saving is $500 million.
       B. The budget deficit is $100 million.
       C. The budget deficit is $500 million.
      D. Public saving is $100 million.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
D

15.    Country Bee has $30,000 of capital per worker, while country Gee has $7,500 of capital per worker.
       According to the standard model of economic growth, additional units of capital will increase output
       ____ in Bee compared to in Gee, holding other factors constant.
      A. more
       B.  less
       C.  not at all
      D. by the same amount
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
B

16.    Consider a closed economy described by the following equations, where Y is national income (or
      GDP), C is consumption, I is investment, G is government purchases, and T is net taxation (taxes
       minus transfers to households):

           Y = C + I + G        Y = 5,000

            C = 500 + 0.75 (Y–T)     T = 1,000     G = 500

         In this economy, investment (I) will be equal to:

      A. 500
       B. 1000
       C. 1500
      D. 2000
       E. 2500
B

17.    Which of the following is NOT a way of calculating GDP?
      A. Sum up the household income of all households living in the country.
       B. Sum up the dollar value of all intermediate goods produced in the country.
       C. Sum up the value-added by all firms in the country.
      D. Sum up the dollar value of all the sales of final goods and services in the country.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
B




                                                                                                5

18.    The graph below represents the loanable funds market of a country. Which of the following may
       cause a move from the equilibrium point marked ‘d’ to the equilibrium point marked ‘a’?





      A. The government budget goes from deficit to surplus; while household confidence falls, causing
           households to cut down on their plans for buying new homes.
       B. The government budget goes from deficit to surplus; while business confidence rises, causing
            business to increase their plans for expansion.
       C. The government budget goes from surplus to deficit; while household confidence falls, causing
           households to cut down on their plans for buying new homes.
      D. The government budget goes from surplus to deficit; while business confidence rises, causing
            business to increase their plans for expansion.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
D

19.    Consider a closed economy where the government budget is in balance (G = T). Suppose the
       government were to reduce spending and taxes by the same amount, keeping the budget balanced. In
        the long run, this will:

      A. Decrease private investment.
       B.  Increase private investment.
       C.  Increase the interest rate.
      D. Not change private savings.
       E. Not change total investment.
B

20.      If two countries have similar population, production and consumption, but citizens in one country
       have longer work hours and less leisure time, then:
      A. Both GDP per capita and economic well-being will be higher in the country with less leisure
           time
       B. Both GDP per capita and economic well-being will be lower in the country with less leisure
            time.
       C. The level of GDP per capita will be the same in both countries, but economic well-being will be
           lower in the country with less leisure time.
      D. Economic well-being will be the same in both countries, but the level of GDP per capita will be
           higher in the country with less leisure time.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
C





                                                                                                6

21.    Over the last 30 years, the private household savings rate in China has been steadily increasing.  If
        the private household savings rate in a country increases, which of the following will happen as a
         result?

      A. Domestic Real Interest Rates will increase.
       B. Domestic Investment will increase.
       C. Marginal Propensity to Consume will increase.
      D. The Stock Market will crash.
       E. None of the above answers are correct
B

22.   Remember that the M2 money multiplier (M2/M0), depends on the currency deposit ratio, as well as
        the required reserve ratio. Suppose that the use of credit cards has reduced the amount of cash that
       people wish to hold, that is the currency deposit ratio drops. This causes:

      A.  the required reserve ratio to increase.
       B.  the nominal money supply to decrease.
       C.  the money multiplier to increase.
      D.  the central bank to buy government bonds.
       E. None of the above are correct.
C

23.     In order to examine a country’s economic growth over time (i.e. how the citizens’ living standards
       have been improving), economists usually look at:
      A. nominal GDP adjusted for unemployment.
       B. nominal GDP per capita.
       C.  real GDP adjusted for unemployment.
      D.  real GDP per capita.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
D

24.   GDP excludes important factors that affect people’s economic well-being, such as the value of:

      A. Fresh air, clear skies, greenery, and a clean environment.
       B. Government provision of services and infrastructure spending.
       C.  Final goods purchased by firms, not households.
      D. Goods produced domestically, but sold to foreigners.
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
A

25.    Which of the following actions will NOT decrease nominal money supply?
      A. Consumers lose confidence in banks and withdraw their money from their bank accounts,
           keeping their money in cash.
       B. The Central Bank sells some foreign currency on the open market.
       C. The government increases government taxation, increasing the size of the budget surplus.
      D. The Central Bank raises the required reserve ratio.
       E. Commercial banks feel uncertain about the future and keep more excess reserves.
C

26.    Because the real interest rate tends to stay relatively constant, interest rates tend to display the Fisher
        Effect over time. That is, nominal interest rates have a tendency to ______ when ____ rises.
      A.  increase ; inflation
       B.  decrease ; inflation
       C.  increase ; unemployment
      D. decrease ; unemployment
       E. None of the above answers are correct.

                                                                                                7

A


27.    Which of the following will definitely decrease the amount of private investment in a closed
      economy where savings is equal to investment?
      A. The government increases government spending and decreases taxation.
       B. The government decreases government spending and increases taxation.
       C. A housing boom causes households to borrow more money for housing investment.
      D. Households decrease the share of their disposable income (Y-T) used for consumption.
       E. None of the above answers are correct
A

28.     Ophelia's farms sold 400 tons of wheat in the year 2006 and 450 tons of wheat in the year 2007. The
        price of a ton of wheat was $200 in 2006 and $220 in 2007. If the year 2006 is the base year,
        Ophelia's contribution to real GDP in 2006 was _____, and in 2007 it was _____.
      A. $80,000; $88,000
       B.  $80,000; $90,000
       C.  $80,000; $99,000
      D. $88,000; $90,000
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
B

29.    According to the standard model of economic growth, holding other factors (such as capital and
        land) constant, a larger population and larger workforce, tends to _____ total output and to _____
       average labor productivity.
      A.  increase; decrease
       B.  increase; increase
       C.  increase; keep unchanged
      D. decrease; increase
       E. None of the above answers are correct.
A

30.    The president of Zambini has recently begun to seize factories belonging to his political opponents,
       and he has given the factories to his friends. His friends don't know much about running factories.
      The courts in Zambini have ruled that the seizures are illegal, but the president has ignored the
         rulings. Because of these actions, we would expect that the growth rate in Zambini will

      A.  increase temporarily as new owners will work harder than the old owners.
       B.  increase permanently because the total amount of human capital in the country will increase as
            the new owners learn how to run the factories.
       C.  not be affected unless the president’s friends are not as smart as his political opponents.
      D.  fall temporarily, but will return to normal when the new owners learn how to run the factories.
       E.  fall and remain lower for a long time, as people know that property rights and the rule of law are
           not respected.
E
